slides.say: A code has four digits. Each digit is from zero to nine, digits may repeat, and the code may start with zero. How many codes contain the digit five at least once?
So they ask for at least once. Like in the lesson, that's our signal for all minus none.
Let's solve it the math way. Why all minus none? The opposite of at least one five is no five at all, and no five is one easy count.
All the codes first. Each of the four digits has ten options. Ten times ten times ten times ten is ten thousand.
at: Ten times ten times ten times ten

slides.say: Now the codes with no five. Each digit has nine options, every digit except five. That's nine times nine times nine times nine, nine to the power of four.
at: nine to the power of four

slides.say: Nine squared is eighty-one. And nine to the power of four is eighty-one times eighty-one.
Eighty-one times eighty is six thousand four hundred eighty. And one more eighty-one is six thousand five hundred sixty-one.
Careful, six thousand five hundred sixty-one is choice number three. It's the codes with no five, not our answer yet.
All minus none. Ten thousand minus six thousand five hundred sixty-one is three thousand four hundred thirty-nine.
Why not count directly? Put a five in the first place, then ten, ten, ten. That's a thousand codes. Four places, four thousand. That's choice number one.
But the code five five zero zero was counted twice, once for the first place and once for the second.
And two thousand nine hundred sixteen is four times nine to the power of three. That counts exactly one five. But at least once also includes two, three and four fives.
Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
